scenes.title: Snowfall in Whispering Forest
scenes.text: One chilly morning, soft snowflakes began falling across the Whispering Forest. Winter was just around the corner, and Poko the Panda knew he had to prepare before everything was covered in snow.
scenes.speaker: STORYBOOK NARRATOR

scenes.title: Honey Cave & The Organizer Board
scenes.text: Poko walked into his cozy little home, "Honey Cave," and opened his magical Forest Organizer Board. This magical board helped him remember everything he owned, so he would never lose anything during winter.
scenes.speaker: STORYBOOK NARRATOR

scenes.title: Poko's Information
scenes.text:
The first thing Poko wrote was his own information.

"My name is Poko. I am 8 years old, my weight is 98.8 kg, and my height is 1.42 meters. Luckily, I am healthy, so today I feel ready for adventure!"
scenes.speaker: POKO THE PANDA

scenes.title: Counting Winter Supplies
scenes.text:
Next, Poko checked his winter food supplies. He counted 18 fresh apples, 42 bamboo sticks, 5 honey jars, 12 carrots, and 86 crunchy nuts.

Smiling, he said,

"Now I have enough food for many snowy days!"
scenes.speaker: POKO THE PANDA

scenes.title: Outside the Cabin
scenes.text: After counting his food, Poko looked at the big water barrel outside his cabin. It still had 2.5 liters of clean water, while the cabin stayed warm at a comfortable 18.5°C.
scenes.speaker: STORYBOOK NARRATOR

scenes.title: The Treasure Chest
scenes.text: Poko then opened his treasure chest. Inside, he happily counted 250 Golden Forest Coins. Looking at his adventure meter, he noticed his energy level was 95, and because everything was going so well, his mood was "Happy."
scenes.speaker: STORYBOOK NARRATOR

scenes.title: Packing the Travel Bag
scenes.text: Before leaving, he packed his favorite meal, "Fresh Bamboo," into his travel bag. His backpack could carry up to 25 kg, so he carefully packed only what he needed.
scenes.speaker: STORYBOOK NARRATOR

scenes.title: Around the Cabin
scenes.text:
As he walked around the cabin one last time, he checked that there were 6 storage boxes neatly arranged in the corner and 35 firewood logs stacked beside the fireplace.

Since tomorrow would be another busy day, Poko planned to sleep for 10 hours that night to stay strong.
scenes.speaker: STORYBOOK NARRATOR

scenes.title: Bobo's Visit
scenes.text:
Just then, his best friend Bobo arrived and asked,

"Wow, Poko! How do you remember so many different things?"

Poko smiled and pointed toward his magical Forest Organizer Board.

"Everything has its own special name, and every name stores something important. Whenever something changes, I simply update it. That's how I never forget anything."
scenes.speaker: BOBO & POKO

scenes.title: Everything Has Its Place
scenes.text:
As the snow gently covered the forest, Poko looked proudly at his organized board.

Everything had its own place.
Everything had its own name.
Everything had its own information.

Now it was your turn to help Poko organize, identify, update, and manage everything inside his magical organizer.
scenes.speaker: STORYBOOK NARRATOR

steps.subtitle: Before winter begins, Poko visits the magical Butterfly Memory Garden to keep track of everything important.
steps.description:
Every colorful butterfly carries one important piece of information. To help Poko remember everything easily, each butterfly wears its own special name.

Now explore the Butterfly Memory Garden and discover how every butterfly safely remembers something important for Poko.

steps.title: Questions: Managing Poko's Organizer (Part 1)
steps.subtitle: Help Poko manage his information records! (Questions 1-4)

bank.title: Question 1: Updating Poko's Water Record
bank.question: Poko drank some water after a long walk through Whispering Forest. Which record on his organizer board should he update?
bank.explanation: Since Poko drank water, he needs to update the 'water' record to reflect his new water level!

bank.title: Question 2: Checking the Weight Record
bank.question: Poko steps onto a wooden scale and opens the page named 'weight' in his organizer. What information should he see stored there?
bank.explanation: The record named 'weight' stores Poko's body weight, which is 98.8 kg!

bank.title: Question 3: Counting Bamboo Sticks
bank.question: Poko counts his winter food stack and sees 42 whole bamboo sticks. How is the number 42 stored in his organizer?
bank.explanation: Whole count numbers like 42 bamboo sticks are whole numbers (Integers)!

bank.title: Question 4: Counting Forest Coins
bank.question: Inside his treasure chest, Poko counts 250 Golden Forest Coins. Which type of value is used for whole counts like 250?
bank.explanation: Counting whole objects like 250 coins uses an Integer!

steps.title: Activity 2: Continue Poko's Organizer
steps.subtitle: Assign each stored detail into the correct special name slot on Poko's board!

steps.title: Questions: Data Types & Values (Part 2)
steps.subtitle: Help Poko identify measurements, text, and status values! (Questions 5-10)

bank.title: Question 5: Water Measurement
bank.question: Poko measures the water level in his outdoor barrel and finds exactly 2.5 Liters of clean water remaining. What type of number is 2.5?
options: Float (a measurement number with a decimal point)
bank.explanation: Numbers with decimal points like 2.5 Liters are Float measurement numbers!

bank.title: Question 6: Cabin Temperature
bank.question: Poko checks the wooden thermometer inside Honey Cave and reads 18.5°C. Why is 18.5 stored as a Float?
options: Because it contains a decimal point representing a precise temperature measurement
Because it is a whole count of coins
Because it is written in text quotation marks
Because it is a True or False answer
bank.explanation: Continuous measurements like 18.5°C contain decimal points and are stored as Floats!

bank.title: Question 7: Poko's Current Mood
bank.question: Poko writes his mood as "Happy" on his organizer board. What type of information is text wrapped in quotes?
bank.explanation: Words and text wrapped in quotation marks like "Happy" are Strings!

bank.title: Question 8: Health Status
bank.question: The Forest Doctor confirms Poko is healthy, so Poko records `healthy = True`. What type of value is `True`?
options: Boolean (a logical True or False value)
bank.explanation: True and False are Boolean values!

bank.title: Question 9: Home Record Page
bank.question: When Poko opens the organizer page labeled `home`, what stored information does he find?
bank.explanation: The record labeled `home` stores the text value "Honey Cave"!

bank.title: Question 10: Best Friend Record
bank.question: Poko wants to check who his best friend is. He looks at the label `friend`. What value is stored under `friend`?
bank.explanation: The label `friend` stores his best friend's name, "Bobo"!

steps.title: 📖 Concept Discovery: How Poko Writes Records (=)
steps.subtitle: How Poko connects a special name to its information using the equal sign (=)

pages.heading: Rule 1: Special Name goes on the LEFT
pages.content: On Poko's organizer board, the special name (like home or water) always sits on the left side of the equal sign.

pages.heading: Rule 2: Equal Sign (=) Connects the Name to Information
pages.content: The equal sign (=) stores the information on the right into the special name on the left.

pages.heading: Rule 3: Stored Information goes on the RIGHT
pages.content: The information item (like 250 coins or "Honey Cave") sits on the right side of the equal sign.

breakdown.explanation: The carved wooden label plaque on Poko's board.
Connecting the information to the name.

friend = "Bobo"

steps.title: Questions: Creating Records with =
steps.subtitle: Help Poko write record statements correctly! (Questions 11-14)

bank.title: Question 11: Storing Honey Jars
bank.question: In Poko's organizer, how does he write a record to store his 5 honey jars in code?
bank.explanation: Correct! `name = value` is how Poko writes a record statement.

bank.title: Question 12: Left Side Naming Rule
bank.question: True or False: In Python, `apples = 18` is valid, but `18 = apples` is INVALID.
bank.explanation: True! The special name MUST be written on the left side of the equal sign.

bank.title: Question 13: Storing Energy Level
bank.question: Which Python statement correctly records Poko's energy level of 95?
bank.explanation: Correct! `energy = 95` stores 95 into the special name 'energy'.

bank.title: Question 14: Assigning Water Level
bank.question: Assign the value 2.5 Liters into the record `water`:
bank.explanation: Great job! `water = 2.5` connects 2.5 Liters of water to the name 'water'.

steps.title: Questions: Updating Poko's Records
steps.subtitle: Test your understanding of updating stored information! (Questions 15-18)

bank.title: Question 15: Overwriting Energy Values
bank.question: Poko rests after chopping firewood and his energy increases from 90 to 95. When he runs `energy = 95`, what happens to his old energy level?
options: The new value 95 overwrites the old value
bank.explanation: Correct! Re-assigning a record overwrites the previous value with the new value.

bank.title: Question 16: Sequential Firewood Updates
bank.question:
Poko looks at his log notes:
`firewood = 30`
`firewood = 35`
What is stored under `firewood` at the end?
bank.explanation: Correct! The second update `firewood = 35` changes the value of `firewood` to 35.

bank.title: Question 17: Updating Forest Coins
bank.question: Poko starts his day with 200 coins and earns more: `coins = 250`. What value is stored in `coins` now?
bank.explanation: Updating `coins = 250` replaces 200 with 250 in memory!

bank.title: Question 18: Updating Poko's Mood
bank.question: If Poko checks his mood: `mood = "Calm"` and then updates `mood = "Happy"`, what is his mood now?
bank.explanation: Updating `mood = "Happy"` changes Poko's mood to "Happy"!

steps.title: Questions: Fixed vs Changing Records
steps.subtitle: Classify values into fixed constants and changing records! (Questions 19-22)

bank.title: Question 19: Hours in a Day
bank.question: Poko notes that there are always 24 hours in a day, but his energy level changes throughout the day. What is hours in a day?
options: A Constant (a value that never changes)
bank.explanation: Correct! Values that stay fixed are Constants, while values that change are Variables!

bank.title: Question 20: Naming Constants
bank.question: Poko's height is 1.42 meters, which stays fixed. How are fixed constant values usually named in Python?
bank.explanation: True! Python programmers use ALL_CAPS for constant naming conventions.

bank.title: Question 21: Daily Changing Detail
bank.question: Which of Poko's details is most likely to change daily during his adventure?
options: The number of hours in a day
bank.explanation: Energy level changes daily as Poko explores and rests!

bank.title: Question 22: Purpose of Special Names
bank.question: Why does Poko use special names for information that changes?
options: So he can update the stored value whenever something changes
So his organizer never lets him open it
Because numbers cannot be written without names
bank.explanation: Special names allow Poko to update and retrieve changing information whenever needed!

steps.title: Questions: Naming Rules for Poko's Records
steps.subtitle: Check which record names follow Python rules! (Questions 23-26)

bank.title: Question 23: Invalid Digit Start Check
bank.question: Poko wants to name a record for his 6 storage boxes. Which name is INVALID because it starts with a number?
bank.explanation: Record names in Python CANNOT start with a number!

bank.title: Question 24: Python Naming Conventions
bank.question: Which name is standard in Python for Poko's favorite food?
bank.explanation: Python uses snake_case with lowercase letters and underscores between words!

bank.title: Question 25: Invalid Space Check
bank.question: Which record name is INVALID because it contains a space?
bank.explanation: Record names CANNOT contain spaces!

bank.title: Question 26: Case Sensitivity Check
bank.question: In Python, are `Poko_Weight` and `poko_weight` treated as the same record?
options: No, Python is case-sensitive, so they are two different records
bank.explanation: Python is case-sensitive! Capital letters create distinct variable names.

steps.title: Observation: Types of Information in Poko's Organizer
steps.subtitle: Observe how different details require different types of records.

questions.prompt: Poko has 6 storage boxes 📦. Which type of value represents whole numbers like 6?
questions.explanation: Correct! Whole count numbers like 6 boxes are Integers (int).

questions.prompt: Poko measures his height: 1.42 meters 📏. Which type of value represents decimal numbers like 1.42?
questions.explanation: Right! Decimal measurement quantities like 1.42 meters are Float numbers.

questions.prompt: Poko checks if he is healthy: `healthy = True`. What data type is `True`?
options: Boolean (logical truth value: True or False)
questions.answer: Boolean (logical truth value: True or False)
questions.explanation: Spot on! True and False are Boolean values (bool).

steps.title: Questions: Four Types of Information (int, float, str, bool)
steps.subtitle: Help Poko classify his organizer records! (Questions 27-30)

bank.title: Question 27: Poko's Age Record
bank.question: Poko records his age as `poko_age = 8`. What data type is `8`?
bank.explanation: 8 is a whole number without decimals or quotes, making it an Integer.

bank.title: Question 28: Poko's Weight Record
bank.question: Poko records his weight as `weight = 98.8`. What data type is `98.8`?
bank.explanation: 98.8 contains a decimal point, making it a Float number.

bank.title: Question 29: Poko's Home Record
bank.question: Poko records his home as `home = "Honey Cave"`. What data type is `"Honey Cave"`?
bank.explanation: "Honey Cave" is wrapped in quotes, making it a String.

bank.title: Question 30: Poko's Health Status
bank.question: Poko records his health status as `healthy = True`. What data type is `True`?
bank.explanation: `True` is a Boolean data type.

steps.title: 📖 Python Connection: Managing Poko's Organizer
steps.subtitle: Writing scripts with multiple records and operations

breakdown.explanation: Storing integer coins and float water level together.

steps.fullCodeExample:
# Multiple records & operations
coins = 250
water = 2.5
healthy = True

coins = coins + 50
print("Forest Coins:", coins)
print("Water Level:", water)

steps.title: Questions: Updating & Printing Poko's Records
steps.subtitle: Test your understanding of updating and printing records! (Questions 31-34)

bank.title: Question 31: Apple Addition
bank.question: Poko has 18 apples and collects 5 more: `apples = 18 + 5`. What is stored in `apples` now?
bank.explanation: Correct! 18 + 5 = 23. The record `apples` is updated to 23.

bank.title: Question 32: Printing Poko's Name
bank.question: What does `print(poko_name)` output if `poko_name = "Poko"`?
bank.explanation: `print(poko_name)` displays the value stored inside the record (`Poko`).

bank.title: Question 33: Spending Forest Coins
bank.question: Poko has 250 coins and spends 50: `coins = 250 - 50`. What is stored in `coins`?
bank.explanation: 250 - 50 = 200. The record `coins` is updated to 200.

bank.title: Question 34: String Quotes Check
bank.question: If Poko writes `home = Honey Cave` without quotation marks, what will Python do?
options: Throw a NameError because String text must be wrapped in quotes!
bank.explanation: Correct! Without quotes, Python looks for a variable named Honey Cave and throws a NameError!
